items.description: Ruins of a vast imperial Roman public bath complex completed in the early 3rd century AD.

Historic cemetery in Testaccio where many foreign artists and writers are buried, including Keats and Shelley.

Triumphal arch near the Colosseum dedicated in 315 AD to Emperor Constantine.
Ancient Roman market complex built into the Quirinal Hill, now housing the Museum of the Imperial Fora.

Church in Rome known for its 9th-century Byzantine-style mosaics.

Palace and private art gallery with a large collection of paintings and lavish period rooms.
Museum in Rome displaying a collection of historical musical instruments.

items.english_name: Museo della Liberazione (Museum of the Liberation of Rome)
items.description: Museum on Rome's resistance and liberation during World War II, housed in a former SS detention site.

items.english_name: Palazzo Massimo alle Terme (National Roman Museum)
items.description: Branch of the National Roman Museum with ancient Roman sculpture, frescoes and mosaics.
Museum within part of the ancient Baths of Diocletian complex, part of the National Roman Museum.

items.english_name: Palazzo Barberini (National Gallery of Ancient Art)
items.description: Baroque palace housing the National Gallery of Ancient Art's collection of paintings.
Historic palace on the Quirinal Hill, the official residence of the President of Italy.
Historic Roman palace with a private art gallery, open to visitors on limited days.
Exhibition hall on Via Nazionale hosting rotating art and cultural exhibitions.
Former papal stables on the Quirinal Hill used as a venue for art exhibitions.
Small villa in Villa Torlonia park, known for its stained glass, now a museum.
Ancient Roman altar dedicated to the goddess Pax, housed in a modern museum building.
Underground early Christian burial catacombs on Via Salaria, visited by guided tour.
Early Christian catacombs beside the Basilica of Sant'Agnese fuori le mura, visited by guided tour.
Monumental staircase connecting Piazza di Spagna with Trinità dei Monti church.
Renaissance villa on the Pincian Hill, home to the French Academy in Rome, with gardens open to visitors.
